content: Dr. Adenike O. Eketunde, MD, MPH, is a medical professional with a diverse background in clinical practice, research, and public health. She can be reached via email at nike10eket@gmail.com. Dr. Eketunde has contributed to the medical literature by authoring pages on topics such as choledocholithiasis, peliosis hepatis, and vomiting in children. Her educational background includes foundational studies in Basic Science at Igbinedion University from 2011 to 2013. She earned her Doctor of Medicine degree from Windsor University School of Medicine in Saint Kitts and Nevis, where she studied from 2013 to 2017. Additionally, she pursued a Master’s degree in Public Health at the University of Massachusetts, Lowell, from 2018 to 2020. Dr. Eketunde has gained clinical experience in various capacities. She worked as a Pathology Assistant at SiParadigm from October 2020 to December 2020. Her clinical training includes core and elective clerkships at Joseph N. France General Hospital in Saint Kitts and Nevis from July 2015 to August 2017. She also completed a clinical externship at Vascular and Vein Associates in Methuen, Massachusetts, from March 2019 to August 2019. She holds several licenses and certifications, including CPR and AED certification, Basic Life Support (BLS) for Healthcare Providers, and certifications in Bloodborne Pathogens and COVID-19 Contact Tracing (offered by Johns Hopkins University via Coursera). She has also earned certificates in areas such as immuno-oncology, molecular testing for colorectal cancer, and global health improvement through HarvardX. Additionally, she is certified in HIPAA compliance, harassment prevention, and the protection of human research participants. Dr. Eketunde is a Certified Clinical Research Professional. Dr. Eketunde has authored several dissertations, including: A Review of the Indications, Techniques, and Complications of Male Urethral Catheterization for General Medical Practice, published on September 24, 2020. A Review of Postmortem Findings in Patients With COVID-19, published on August 27, 2020. Diabetes as a Risk Factor for Breast Cancer, published on May 7, 2020. She has also delivered presentations, such as serving as the lead presenter on the topic Impact of Social Media on Health Promotion in Sub-Saharan Africa at the 22nd Annual Student Research and Community Engagement Symposium held at the University of Massachusetts, Lowell, in May 2019. Dr. Eketunde has been recognized for her academic and professional achievements, including receiving honors from the Zuckerberg College of Health Science for Interprofessional Education.
